title: The Difference Between Blog Article and Community/Member Article | Brilliant Directories Documentation | BD Support
content: The Difference Between Blog Article and Community/Member Article Link: https://support.brilliantdirectories.com/support/solutions/articles/12000034913 The website comes with two article post types. Blog Article Community/Member Article These are similar post types but with a few differences, specifically for the Blog post type. Blog Article How to Add a Blog Post The default Permalink URL is: /blog This post type is intended for curated articles created only by the Site Administrator or designated Blog Contributors, not by regular members of the directory. This is because the Blog Articles have the "Featured on Homepage?" option: Featured Blog Article Slider This add-on allows the website admin to select and manage which Blog articles are featured on the homepage slider, which can display up to five posts. If this setting is enabled for all members and profiles, it becomes difficult to control which posts are displayed. Custom SEO Data There are also additional Custom SEO Data fields available. These fields are only available to the admin for two reasons: This ensures each post can have SEO data tailored to the individual post instead of being tied to the overall post type. How To Edit The SEO Settings Of Dynamic (Search Results) Pages This prevents harmful or false data from being entered, which could damage the website’s SEO and result in lower search engine rankings. Adding Images to Blog Articles When adding images to blog articles, this post type uses the Media Manager to store uploads. Both the cover image and any files added through the Froala Editor are saved in a designated folder, keeping everything organized on the admin side. My Content » Media Manager Because the Media Manager is the central storage tool for site images, this post type is meant for admin use only. Allowing all users to upload here could lead to unnecessary or low-quality files, so keeping it limited to admins ensures the Media Manager stays clean and reliable. Community/Member Article How to Post an Article The default Permalink URL is: /articles This post type is intended for members use only. This post type does not include the ‘ Featured on Homepage ’ option or Custom SEO fields.
